LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.

3.– WORKSHEET: WHERE DO I PUT IT? (P.10) (8’)
P&P S2 | Page 10
Where Do I Put It?
10
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
MATERIALS
•	 P&P Story 2 Page 10 Stickers
This worksheet shows a picture of a fridge full of food and 
drinks. Your Ss will get some stickers which they have to place 
on the page following your instructions.
Start by reviewing the names of the items in the fridge. Say, 
“My fridge is full of food. What is there inside?”. Using your 
finger, encourage the Ss to respond, “There are some yoghurts, 
some watermelon, strawberries, there is also some turkey, 
some salami, a chicken, etc.”
Before giving out the stickers, review the vocabulary by saying, 
“Look! I went shopping today and I got a courgette, two onions,

an aubergine, some cheese, some eggs, and some cherries. 
Shall we put the food in the fridge?”
Then do the following dictation:
•	 Put the cheese next to the yoghurts.
•	 Put the cherries between the turkey and the 
strawberries.
•	 Put the eggs under the turkey.
•	 Put the aubergine next to the sausages.
•	 Put the courgette next to the lettuce and under the 
aubergine.
•	 Put the onions under the eggs.
To review, ask Ss about the rest of the items found in the 
fridge by saying for example, “The yoghurts are between the 
watermelons and the cheese.” or “The milk is under the carrots.”

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 2, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 7 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic.
The point of this activity is to review the places in town in a 
fun way using the sticker pages. Ss have to look at the stickers 
and spot the differences between the two maps. Model the 
task with your Ss by looking for the stickers, sticking them, 
and answering the questions.
Have Ss open pp.18-19 (sticker pages section) and say, “Let’s 
spot the differences in these two maps!”. Point to square 
number 23 and ask, “What number is this?”, to which Ss should 
respond, “It’s number 23!”. Say, “Can you find number 23 on 
the sheet? What is it?”, and elicit, “Here it is! It’s the bank!”. 
Have Ss place the sticker and ask them, “On which map is 
the bank next to the clothes shop?”, eliciting the response 
“On map number 1!”. You can ask them to point at the map to 
ensure comprehension.
Continue in this manner and stick as many stickers as time 
allows, but don’t worry if you can’t finish the whole page. Tell 
the Ss that they can continue at home.
KEY (From left to right)
Sticker 23: On which map is the bank next to the clothes 
shop? On map number 1.
Sticker 24: On which map is the hairdresser’s opposite 
the bank? On map number 2.
Sticker 25: On which map is the sweet shop between the 
gym and the butcher’s? On map number 1.
Sticker 26: On map number 2, is the clothes shop next 
to the café? No, it isn’t. 
Sticker 27: On map number 2, is the supermarket next 
to the gym? No, it isn’t. 
Sticker 28: On map number 2, is the petrol station behind 
the sweet shop? No, it isn’t.

6.– ACTIVITY 4: FOLLOWING DIRECTIONS (5’)
> Warm-Up
Put a red sticker on each Ss’ left hand and a green one on 
their right. Then practise left, right, and straight ahead by using 
your hands. Say, “Turn left!” and have everybody turn to the left 
(you should too; having your back turned to your Ss is helpful, 
so everybody is pointing to the same left). Do the same with 
right and straight ahead.
Gradually say each command faster and faster.
> Main Activity
Next, the Ss should form a line. When you say, “Go straight 
ahead”, they must pat the person in front of them on the head. If 
you say, “Turn left” Ss must pat the left shoulder of the person 
in front of them and if you say, “Turn right”, their right shoulder. 
Finally, get them (still in a line) to follow your instructions 
but walking around the class pretending to be on a train.
> Advanced Groups
If your Ss have understood the concepts quickly, you can 
let them take on the teacher role and give commands to their 
classmates.
7.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (14’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask

them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and do 
the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.

BONUS
ACTIVITY 3: CAN YOU TELL ME THE WAY?
P.2.3
P.2.3
TARGET LANGUAGE
Turn right
Go past
Go straight ahead
Turn left
Behind
On your right
On your left
Opposite
Next to
Between
> How to Play
In this game, the Ss must tell their classmate the correct 
way to get to the shop to buy a certain item.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the name of the items (P.2.3) with the Ss 
and where they can buy them. Ask, “Where can you buy a 
dress?” to which they should answer, “You can buy a dress at 
the clothes shop.” If needed, review the shops on the A3 that 
your Ss find tricky (such as charity shop, town hall, dentist, 
basketball court, football pitch, etc.)
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Pair the Ss up (S1 and S2). Put the Item memory cards (P.2.3) 
face down on the table. To do the activity, proceed as detailed 
below. We highly encourage you to model the steps with a S 
first. Say, “Let’s go explore the city!”. Then proceed as follows: 
•	 S1: Takes a bike cutout and turns over an item card.
•	 T: “What do you need to buy?”
•	 S1: “I need to buy dog food.” (or whatever item is on 
the card). 
•	 T: “Where can you buy dog food?”
•	 S2: “You can buy dog food at the pet shop.”

•	 T: “S1, you are at the bookshop.”
•	 S1: “Can you tell me the way (to the pet shop), please?”
•	 S2: Gives directions accordingly. For example: “To get 
to the pet shop, turn right. Go straight ahead and go 
past the supermarket and the sports centre. At the 
sports centre turn left. You will find the pet shop on 
your right / the pet shop is opposite the charity shop.”
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss about the location of different shops. For example: 
“John, where is the greengrocer’s?” to which they should reply, 
“The greengrocer’s is between the bakery and the charity 
shop.”
ACTIVITY 8: TAKE A WALK (VERSION 1) (TR#14)
P.2.3
> How to Play
This version of this activity is played like the musical chairs 
game.
> Warm-Up
Place the A3 Map (P.2.3) in the middle of the table and do a 
little warm-up by saying “If you find the charity shop, point it 
out to me!” and have all your Ss point to the right place on the 
map. Continue in this manner until you have gone over some 
of the shops that are mentioned in the song.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s take a walk around 
town!”. Leave the map on the table and play the song Take a 
Walk Version 1 (TR#14). The Ss should walk around the table 
singing the song but, when you pause the track after each 
shop, the first S to point to the correct shop on the map should 
sit down so that the rest of their classmates can have a go at 
this activity as well.

> Follow-Up
If time allows, ask each S, “What can you buy at the...?” 
and the Ss individually, each saying a different item, should 
say, “You can buy ... at the...”. Challenge them to come up with 
items they haven’t learned in class.
